title: Modified Bradford Procedure for Residual Protein Testing in Enzyme Catalysis
author: Yongbo Cui
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k4kcyuw
materials: Standard Solution Extraction: The standard solutions are extracted with an organic:aqueous phase ratio of 2:1. Then 150 µL of each protein sample solution in organic reagent and 75 µL of aqueous phase like dH2O were charged to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube. Each solution was vortexed for at least 1 minute and centrifuged for 10 minutes at max krpm to achieve phase separation. The aqueous phase was separated from the organic phase for assay via Bradford in triplicate.

steps.title: Prepare Standard Residual Protein
steps.instruction: Prepare a standard residual protein, such as BSA or the purified enzyme used for product synthesis.

substeps.instruction: Determine the pure protein content using the common Bradford method or SEC-HPLC.

steps.title: Create Standard Protein Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare a series of standard residual protein solutions using a water buffer and organic reagent.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve the standard residual protein in a water buffer (e.g., the enzyme soluble buffer used for catalytic reaction) to a final content, such as 1 mg/mL.
Perform accurate dilutions, preferably in capacity bottles, to create a series of standard solutions.
Use an organic reagent (free of protein) that is fully miscible with the aqueous solution as the dilution buffer.

steps.title: Perform Bradford Assay
steps.instruction: Determine the protein content of the aqueous phase samples (expected concentrations ~100-600 µg/mL) following the Bradford procedure.

substeps.instruction: Blend each sample aqueous solution with room temperature Coomassie Plus Protein assay reagent at a 1:50 ratio.
Incubate the reactions for 10 to 60 minutes at room temperature.
Measure the absorbance of the resulting solution at 595 nm using a spectrophotometer or Microplate Reader.

steps.title: Analyze Data and Create Calibration Curve
steps.instruction: Process the absorbance data to quantify protein content.

substeps.instruction: Average the absorbance values of the standard solutions and normalize them against the 0 µg/mL protein control.
Create a calibration curve using no less than (NLT) 6 evenly spaced points.
Ensure the calibration curve fits a linear regression with an Rsq value of NLT 0.99.
